1 مَصَتَ , ([aor.
مَصُتَ ,] inf. n. مَصْتٌ TA,) Inivit puellam: [K:) dial. form of مصَدَ. (TA.) ―
-b2- مَصَتَ النَّاقَةَ He laid hold upon the womb of the camel, and put in his hand, and extracted the water [i. e. the semen injected into it]. (M, K.) [See also مَسَطَ.] ―
-b3- مَصَتَ المِعَى He squeezed out what was in the intestine, or gut, with his fingers. (TA.) ―
-b4- مَصَتَ It (herbage) purged cattle; or relaxed them in the bowels. (Marg. note in a copy of the S.) ―
-b5- مَصَتَ He squeezed an ulcer, so as to express the matter. (Marg. note in a copy of the S) ―
-b6- مَصَتَ He sucked saliva. (Marg. note in a copy of the S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
